preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete maternal medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight for fetal CHD. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard prenatal ultrasound  |  Medium = targeted genetic panel or fetal echo ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = advanced imaging, amniocentesis, or MFM consultation ($1,500–$5,000+)

questions.question: Was the 4-chamber view abnormal (asymmetric chambers, hypoplastic ventricle, or atrioventricular discordance) on anatomic ultrasound at 18–22 weeks?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — 4-chamber abnormality carries ~70–80% PPV for structural CHD and is the primary screening signal

questions.question: Were the outflow tracts (LVOT/RVOT) absent, overriding, or in a transposition pattern on targeted fetal echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — outflow tract views combined with 4-chamber view raise diagnostic sensitivity to >90%

questions.question: Is there nuchal translucency (NT) ≥3.5 mm at 11–14 weeks on first-trimester ultrasound?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — NT ≥3.5 mm is associated with CHD independent of chromosomal anomaly

questions.question: Is there evidence of hydrops fetalis (ascites, pleural effusion, skin edema, or pericardial effusion)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — hydrops signals severe cardiac compromise or structural CHD with high-output failure

questions.question: Is fetal cardiac axis outside the normal 30–60° range (dextrocardia or axis deviation)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — abnormal cardiac axis is an independent ultrasound marker for structural CHD

questions.question: Does the mother or father have a confirmed CHD diagnosis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — parental CHD confers 3–10× recurrence risk over population baseline of ~1%

questions.question: Is there a known genetic syndrome in the family (Down, DiGeorge/22q11, Turner, Noonan, Williams, CHARGE)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — syndrome-linked CHD risk ranges from 25% (Noonan) to 75% (DiGeorge/22q11)

questions.question: Is there a first-degree sibling with a confirmed CHD?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — sibling CHD recurrence risk is 2–3% vs. ~1% population baseline

questions.question: Was a prior pregnancy affected by CHD?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — prior affected pregnancy elevates recurrence risk, especially for left-sided obstructive lesions

questions.question: Does cell-free fetal DNA (cfDNA / NIPT) flag Trisomy 21, 18, 13, or 22q11.2 deletion?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — Trisomy 21: 40–50% CHD rate; Trisomy 18: >90%; 22q11 deletion: ~75% CHD rate

questions.question: Does amniocentesis or CVS karyotype confirm a chromosomal abnormality?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — confirms cfDNA signal and defines the specific aneuploidy for recurrence counseling

questions.question: Does chromosomal microarray identify a pathogenic CNV in a cardiac developmental gene (TBX1, GATA4, NKX2-5, or 22q11.2 locus)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — CNVs in these loci directly implicate cardiac morphogenesis

questions.question: Was lithium used in the first trimester?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — lithium is associated with Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve

questions.question: Was isotretinoin (Accutane) or another retinoic acid derivative used in the first trimester?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — retinoic acid derivatives are among the highest-risk cardiac teratogens (conotruncal defects, aortic arch anomalies)

questions.question: Was there rubella infection or confirmed inadequate rubella immunity in the first trimester?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — first-trimester rubella causes pulmonary artery stenosis and patent ductus arteriosus

questions.question: Was there significant alcohol or cocaine use documented in the social history (first trimester)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — alcohol is associated with VSD and septal defects; cocaine with aortic coarctation

questions.question: Was paroxetine (Paxil) or another SSRI used consistently in the first trimester?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — paroxetine carries a modest but consistent signal for VSD and right-heart defects

questions.question: Is there pregestational Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes with HbA1c >8% in the first trimester?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — pregestational diabetes increases CHD risk 3–5× over baseline; transposition, VSD, and heterotaxy are most common

questions.question: Is there maternal SLE with positive anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB antibodies?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — anti-Ro/SSA antibodies cause congenital complete heart block in 2–3% of exposed fetuses

questions.question: Is there maternal obesity (BMI ≥40) limiting ultrasound anatomic survey quality?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe obesity is an independent modest risk factor and significantly compromises fetal echo sensitivity

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: fetal structural CHD highly probable; immediate referral to pediatric cardiologist and maternal-fetal medicine (MFM); delivery planning at CCHD-capable center with cardiac surgery on site

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: targeted fetal echocardiogram mandatory; MFM consultation indicated; genetic counseling if chromosomal or syndromic CHD suspected

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: background or mildly elevated CHD risk; routine anatomic survey at 18–22 weeks adequate; fetal echo warranted if genetic testing or ultrasound findings evolve during pregnancy
